_note: The sun's times of a day and the periods 14 CFR 1.1, 61.57(b) and 91.209(a) read from them, written down from the U.S. Naval Observatory's tables, never from the code; each tolerance the tables' minute and the solar calculation's accuracy (engine/crates/flight/src/sun.rs's note), wider where the sun grazes the line. Shape and checks as engine/facade/tests/common/cases.rs says; asked by engine/facade/tests/rule_cases.rs.

cases.name: Chicago on the 2026 March equinox: the times of its local day
cases.source: U.S. Naval Observatory, Astronomical Applications, one-day sun data (aa.usno.navy.mil/api/rstt/oneday, tz=0), to the minute: 41.88 N 87.63 W, 2026-03-20 begin civil twilight 11:26, rise 11:54; 2026-03-21 set 00:03, end civil twilight 00:31 (the evening of the 20th, local). Sunrise and sunset the upper limb on the horizon, civil twilight the centre 6 degrees down.

cases.name: Chicago's night, passenger night and lights from the evening of 2026-03-20
cases.source: 14 CFR 1.1 night: end of evening civil twilight to beginning of morning civil twilight; 61.57(b): "the period beginning 1 hour after sunset and ending 1 hour before sunrise"; 91.209(a): "from sunset to sunrise". U.S. Naval Observatory, Astronomical Applications, one-day sun data (aa.usno.navy.mil/api/rstt/oneday, tz=0), to the minute: 2026-03-21 end civil twilight 00:31, set 00:03, begin civil twilight 11:24, rise 11:52.

cases.name: Anchorage at the June solstice: no 1.1 night, but 61.57(b)'s period still runs
cases.source: U.S. Naval Observatory, Astronomical Applications, one-day sun data (aa.usno.navy.mil/api/rstt/oneday, tz=0), to the minute: 61.17 N 150.00 W, 2026-06-21 rise 12:21; 2026-06-22 set 07:42 (the evening of the 21st, local), rise 12:22, "Object continuously above the Twilight Limit". 14 CFR 1.1's night needs civil twilight to end; 61.57(b) reads sunset and sunrise.

cases.name: Utqiagvik at the December solstice: the sun never rises, so lights all day, and a short civil day
cases.source: U.S. Naval Observatory, Astronomical Applications, one-day sun data (aa.usno.navy.mil/api/rstt/oneday, tz=0), to the minute: 71.29 N 156.79 W, 2026-12-21 "Object continuously below the Horizon", begin civil twilight 20:56, end civil twilight 23:55. 91.209(a): sunset to sunrise.

cases.name: Utqiagvik at the June solstice: the sun never sets, so no night and no lights
cases.source: U.S. Naval Observatory, Astronomical Applications, one-day sun data (aa.usno.navy.mil/api/rstt/oneday, tz=0), to the minute: 71.29 N 156.79 W, 2026-06-21 "Object continuously above the Horizon", "Object continuously above the Twilight Limit".
